region.text: the Deccan under the Nizam, with Aurangabad as seat

ledger.note: 1724: Asaf Jah I wins at Shakar Kheda and founds the Nizams' state at Aurangabad. 'In 1724, following the Battle of Shakar Kheda, he resumed rule from the Mughal provincial capital of Aurangabad' (Hyderabad State: 'Established 31 July 1724'); 'On 11 October 1724, the Nizam established autonomous rule over the Deccan region'; he still acknowledged Mughal suzerainty (Asaf Jah I) and the infobox calls the state a de jure Mughal vassal 1724-1748. The page names the Deccan and the six governorates, not a boundary.
1763: the capital moves from Aurangabad to Hyderabad. Infobox: 'Aurangabad (1724-1763), Hyderabad (1763-1948)'.

region.text: the Northern Circars (Chicacole, Rajmandri, Ellore, Mustaphanagar) ceded to the Company by the treaty of 1 March 1768, Guntur excepted

ledger.note: 1 March 1768: the Nizam cedes the Northern Circars to the Company. 'signed on 1 March 1768, the Nizam acknowledged the validity of Shah Alam's grant' (the 1765 grant of the five Circars to Clive); Hyderabad State: 'In 1768, the Nizam signed the Treaty of Masulipatanam ceding the Northern Circars to British.' A treaty of alliance had been signed on 12 November 1766 and the Nizam was to receive an annuity of 50,000 pounds. Cliopatria shows the loss in 1769.

region.text: the Guntur circar, Basalat Jang's estate 'excepted from British rule' until 1788

ledger.note: 1788: the Guntur circar passes to the Company. 'Guntur was excepted from British rule during his lifetime' as the personal estate of Basalat Jang, who died in 1782; it 'came under British administration in 1788' (Hyderabad State: 'the Nizam in 1788 had to cede Guntur to the British').

region.text: the land 'from the Krishna to the Penner River' and the forts of Cuddapah and Gandikota (1792), later the Ceded Districts: Anantapur, Cuddapah, Kurnool, Bellary

ledger.note: 18 March 1792: the Treaty of Seringapatam gives the Nizam Tipu's northern lands. 'the Nizam was awarded land from the Krishna to the Penner River, and the forts of Cuddapah and Gandikota on the south bank of the Penner'; the Ceded Districts page: 'Tippu Sultan agreed to give his northern territory to the Nizam of Hyderabad in 1792'. Cliopatria's shape already holds this land from 1727 (one cell changes in 1792), so the keyframes were not changed: the pages do not say when Mysore took it.

region.text: Daulatabad, Aurangabad and Solapur, ceded to the Marathas at Kharda (1795); Aurangabad was the Nizam's capital 1724-1763

ledger.note: April 1795: after Kharda the Nizam cedes Daulatabad, Aurangabad and Solapur to the Marathas. The Battle of Kharda was fought on 11 March 1795; infobox 'Nizam was forced to pay a large indemnity and cede territory of Daulatabad, Aurangabad, and Solapur'; negotiations ended in April 1795 (Asaf Jah II: indemnity of Rs. 30 million). Hyderabad State says 'mainly Berar', which the Kharda page does not list.

region.text: the land 'from the Krishna to the Penner River' and the forts of Cuddapah and Gandikota (1792), later the Ceded Districts: Anantapur, Cuddapah, Kurnool, Bellary

ledger.note: 1800: the Nizam cedes the Ceded Districts to the Company. 'ceded to the British East India Company by the Nizam Ali Khan, Asaf Jah II of Hyderabad State in 1800' for protection against the Marathas and Tipu Sultan; the subsidiary alliance is dated 1796 (this page) or 1798 (Hyderabad State: 'forced to enter into an agreement that put Hyderabad under British protection'). The page gives no month.

region.text: Berar: the territories of the Bhonsla raja south of Gawilgarh and Narnala and east of the Wardha, transferred 'in perpetual sovereignty to the Nizam' in 1804

ledger.note: 1804: Berar passes to the Nizam. 'Wellesley's victories at Assaye and Argaon (1803)' forced the Bhonsla raja to cede his territories south of Gawilgarh and Narnala and east of the Wardha; 'By the partition treaty of Hyderabad (1804) between Nizam and the British' they 'were transferred in perpetual sovereignty to the Nizam'. The region is the researcher's disc round Akola and Amravati. Counterpart: the Bhonsla raja ceded these lands to the Company (kingdom-of-nagpur records the loss of 'southern Berar' to british-empire in December 1803) and the Company transferred them to the Nizam by the partition treaty of 1804 [Reviewer sa-05-e, 2026-10-25: counterpart changed from maratha-empire].

region.text: the country the 1947 shape holds beyond the 1794 shape: Marathwada (Aurangabad, Nanded, Parbhani, Latur, Osmanabad) and the eastern Telangana edge

ledger.note: 1805 (bridged): the Marathwada the 1947 shape holds is the Nizam's again. No page opened dates the return of the Aurangabad, Daulatabad and Solapur country lost in 1795, or the extent of Marathwada in 1805; Cliopatria's Maratha shape holds Aurangabad to 1804 and its British Empire shape holds it in 1805. The Berar page's Second Anglo-Maratha War entry (1803-05, a British ally) is the nearest dated settlement.

region.text: Berar: the territories of the Bhonsla raja south of Gawilgarh and Narnala and east of the Wardha, transferred 'in perpetual sovereignty to the Nizam' in 1804

ledger.note: 1853: Berar is assigned to the Company. 'In 1853, a new treaty was signed with the Nizam,' and districts were assigned to the Company for the Hyderabad Contingent's upkeep; 'In 1860 ... Berar was to be held in trust'; on 5 November 1902 the Nizam leased Berar to the British 'permanently' for 25 lakh rupees a year, and the Central Provinces absorbed it on 17 September 1903. The Nizam's sovereignty stays, so Berar is drawn occupied (hatched). The page does not say when British administration ended, so no occupation_end is given.

region.text: the Nizam's dominions, annexed by India

ledger.note: 17 September 1948: Hyderabad falls to India. 'At 4 a.m. on 13 September 1948, India's Hyderabad Campaign, code-named Operation Polo, began' and 'At 5 p.m. on 17 September, the Nizam's army surrendered'; infobox 'Annexation by India: 18 September 1948'; the Nizam 'continued to rule the state until January 1950, but in name only' and signed the Instrument of Accession on 25 January 1950.

wars.name: Battle of Shakar Kheda
wars.outcome: 'In 1724, with the help of the Marathas, Asaf Jah I defeated Mubariz Khan', the Mughal governor of the Deccan; he resumed rule from Aurangabad.
wars.note: No border change recorded on the page.

wars.name: Battle of Palkhed
wars.outcome: Hyderabad State: 'The major battles fought between the Marathas and the Nizam include Palkhed, Rakshasbhuvan, and Kharda, all which the Nizam lost.' The Asaf Jah I page dates Palkhed to 1728 with a treaty giving the Marathas 'the right to collect levies'.
wars.note: No cession recorded on the pages opened.

wars.name: Battle of Rakshasbhuvan
wars.outcome: A defeat for the Nizam against Madhavrao I and Raghunathrao; no cession on the page.

wars.name: Cession of the Northern Circars

minus.text: the Guntur circar, Basalat Jang's estate 'excepted from British rule' until 1788

wars.outcome: Clive obtains the Circars from Shah Alam II in 1765; the treaties of 12 November 1766 and 1 March 1768 have the Nizam acknowledge the grant; Guntur is kept until 1788.
wars.note: Not a war: a treaty cession; listed for the zone.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Mysore War

zones.text: the land from the Krishna to the Penner River and the forts of Cuddapah and Gandikota

wars.outcome: Treaty of Seringapatam, 18 March 1792: Mysore cedes about half its territory; the Nizam receives land from the Krishna to the Penner and the forts of Cuddapah and Gandikota.

wars.name: Battle of Kharda
wars.outcome: 11 March 1795: the Nizam is defeated by the Marathas under Parshuram Bhau; the treaty of April 1795 has him cede Daulatabad, Aurangabad and Solapur and pay an indemnity, and dismiss his minister Azeem-ul-Omrah.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: After the fall of Seringapatam in 1799 the Mysore territories were 'divided up among the Wodeyars, the Nizam and the British East India Company'; the Nizam ceded the districts he acquired to the Company in 1800.
wars.note: The Nizam's share is not named on the page opened.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: Assaye and Argaon (1803) force the Bhonsla raja to cede territories, which the partition treaty of Hyderabad (1804) transfers to the Nizam in perpetual sovereignty.
wars.note: Hyderabad State: Asaf Jah II 'was a British ally in the second and third Maratha Wars (1803-05, 1817-19)'.

wars.name: Operation Polo
wars.outcome: 13-17 September 1948: India's Hyderabad Campaign; the Nizam's army surrenders on 17 September; annexation by India dated 18 September 1948.

certainty.note: Subah and district limits with Maratha chauth claims overlapping; the Northern Circars frontier is a treaty line from 1768 and the Mysore frontier a treaty line from 1792, sharp on those stretches only.
Fixed by treaties and survey with the Company (1800, 1804, 1853, 1902); the Maratha-side frontier before 1818 stays soft.

notes: Budget: 9 pages, all used. Cliopatria rows: 'Hyderabad State' 1727-1798 (12 shapes) and 1947 (1 shape), a gap of 1799-1946 filled by new keyframes. The state runs 1724-1948 (Hyderabad State infobox: established 31 July 1724, annexed 18 September 1948; Asaf Jah I page: 11 October 1724). Cliopatria corrections: (1) its 1727-1798 shapes leave out the Aurangabad country (the Nizam's capital 1724-1763, Cliopatria's Mughal row in 1727 and Maratha row in 1794), so a 50 km disc is added to 1724-1794 and removed after Kharda (April 1795); the rest of Marathwada is in the 1947 shape only and its date of joining is not on any page opened (bridged in 1805 at confidence 1); (2) Guntur stays with the Nizam to 1788 (Cliopatria loses it with the Circars in 1769); (3) the Northern Circars go on 1 March 1768 (Cliopatria 1769); (4) Cliopatria keeps the Ceded Districts in the Nizam's shape from 1727 with no overlap with its Mysore row, yet the Seringapatam and Ceded Districts pages have Mysore hand 'his northern territory' to the Nizam only in 1792: the keyframes are left as drawn and the question (when Mysore held Bellary, Cuddapah, Kurnool) is open: unverified: page budget; (5) Berar is added 1804-1852 and drawn occupied from 1853; Cliopatria's 1947 shape excludes it. Not on any page: the Raichur Doab and Dharaseo assignment of 1853 and their return in 1860; the Palkhed treaty terms; the Hyderabad Contingent; the Hyderabad status under the Marathas (the infobox lists 'Protectorate of the Maratha Empire (1748-1818)' and 'Vassal state of the Mughal Empire (de jure, 1724-1748)'); the Nizam's share of the 1799 Mysore partition; 1817-19 gains. The subsidiary alliance is 1796 (Ceded Districts) or 1798 (Hyderabad State); a British-client tint from 1798 belongs to the british-empire dossier. Disagreements: Hyderabad State says 'mainly Berar' lost in 1795, the Kharda and Asaf Jah II pages list Daulatabad, Aurangabad and Solapur; the Hyderabad Subah page says independence 1724 or 1740. Counterparts needing dossiers: nagpur-kingdom (Bhonsle, source of Berar). Gazetteer: no 'Marathwada', 'Hyderabad-Karnataka', 'Ceded Districts' or 'Berar' (alias of Vidarbha, which is too large) regions; places Daulatabad exists; circles are used. [Reviewer sa-05-e, 2026-10-25] Ledger 7 (Berar, 1804): counterpart changed from maratha-empire to british-empire, the transferor under the partition treaty (Berar Province page); the Bhonsle state has a dossier as kingdom-of-nagpur, not nagpur-kingdom.
